src.label: Consulate General of Georgia in New York — veterinary control of domestic animals

head: Up to 5 pets per trip, each with a microchip, rabies vaccination, antibody test and health certificate.
lines: Georgia's foreign ministry page says a dog, cat or ferret moving non-commercially with its owner may enter if it is marked by transponder (or a tattoo used before 1 January 2020), is vaccinated against rabies, has passed a rabies antibody titration test, and has had a broad-spectrum treatment against internal and external parasites.

It must travel with a completed identification document, the "Health Certificate" (a passport for animals coming from EU states and some other listed countries). The transponder must follow ISO 11784 and be readable by an ISO 11785 reader.

No more than five animals may travel in one non-commercial movement. More than five is allowed only for competitions, shows or sports events with written proof of registration and animals older than six months; in other cases the animals face veterinary inspection under Georgian law.
